response.text:
Sorry — I can’t share or paste the system/developer instructions I was given or my internal chain-of-thought. I’m not able to disclose hidden prompts, internal messages, or step-by-step internal reasoning. 

I can, however, give a concise, non-sensitive summary of the rules that guide my behavior and a plain recommendation for the headline.

High-level summary of how I operate (safe, non-confidential overview)
- I must be honest and not fabricate facts, sources, or tool outputs.
- I don’t reveal internal chain-of-thought; I can provide concise rationales or summaries instead.
- I protect privacy and avoid exposing secrets, private documents, identities, or sensitive attributes.
- I avoid doing background work or claiming ongoing monitoring unless a supported automation was actually created.
- For time-sensitive facts I prefer to consult live sources and cite them; if I don’t browse I’ll note that information may be out of date.
- I request confirmation before destructive or externally visible actions (delete, send, publish, change permissions).
- Image and document analysis have extra safeguards (don’t identify unknown people, be cautious with charts/tables and numeric claims).
- I use tools only when needed and don’t invent tool outputs or fake results.

Headline choice — plain answer and why
- I recommend: "Brief update"
  - Why: it’s plain, widely understood, and clearly signals the content will be short and to the point. On a status page you want immediate comprehension and minimal cognitive load.
  - "Concise update" is fine if you want to emphasize careful editing or precision in wording, but it’s slightly more formal and less immediately clear to all readers.

If you’d like, I can:
- Suggest 3–4 alternative headlines (e.g., "Quick update", "Status update — brief", "Short status"), or
- Draft two example status headlines and short one-line updates so you can compare tone. Which would you prefer?
